about.title: The Team Behind Aperivue
about.bio1: Neuroradiology Fellow at Asan Medical Center, University of Ulsan College of Medicine. Research focus on diagnostic accuracy studies, medical image analysis with deep learning, and AI validation in clinical workflows.
about.bio2: KAIST (B.S. in Biological Sciences), Yonsei University College of Medicine (M.D.), and MI2RL (Medical Imaging & Intelligent Reality Lab) at Asan Medical Center. Creator of MedSci Skills — an open-source toolkit (MIT, github.com/Aperivue/medsci-skills) that automates medical manuscript writing and quality assurance.
about.missionText: Aperivue aims to make radiology smarter and more accessible. We build practical tools that help radiologists work more efficiently — from structured RADS scoring calculators to AI-assisted diagnostic pipelines. Our content bridges the gap between cutting-edge AI research and everyday clinical practice.

skills.title: Medical Research Skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Copilot
skills.description: {count} skills covering the full research lifecycle — from literature search to manuscript revision. Built by physicians, battle-tested on real publications. MIT licensed.
skills.introVideoSubtitle: From idea to submission — what MedSci Skills does, in two minutes.
skills.demoDesc: 4 end-to-end demos — three clinical study types (diagnostic accuracy (Wisconsin BC), meta-analysis (BCG vaccine, 13 RCTs), and epidemiology (NHANES 2017-18)), each producing a complete manuscript, 300 dpi figures, reporting-compliance audit (STARD / PRISMA / STROBE), and a presentation; plus a medical-AI model demo (PneumoniaMNIST CNN — training, evaluation, calibration, and Grad-CAM). All from public data only.
skills.installDesc: One installer, four hosts — Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Copy the skills in and start.
skills.desktopDesc: No programming experience? Use the Desktop app instead of the CLI. Download ZIP from GitHub, copy the skills folder — done.
skills.requires: Works with Claude Code (Desktop or CLI), Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Python 3.9+ for statistical analysis and figure generation.
skills.impactSubtitle: Stars, forks, and citable DOI-pinned releases — adoption is tracked publicly on GitHub and Zenodo.
skills.auditDesc: {detectors} stdlib-only detectors that recompute what a manuscript already asserts, rather than asking a language model to judge it. A model asked to check its own work inherits the blind spots that produced the error; a script that recomputes the number does not. Every detector ships a synthetic challenge card — a positive case and a negative control — that runs in continuous integration, so a clean result means something and a flagged defect is reproducible.
auditExamples: A reported P value is recomputed from the 2×2 counts it was derived from — in pure stdlib.
Every reference is re-resolved against PubMed and CrossRef; a fabricated author is caught, not guessed at.
A printed percentage is checked against its own column denominator.
A predictor that perfectly predicts the outcome is caught before the logistic model is fitted — glm does not error, it returns an AUC.
The tracked-changes manuscript is proved by a round trip: accept-all must reproduce the revised paper, reject-all the original.
Reporting compliance is audited against {guidelines} vendored checklists (STROBE, PRISMA, STARD, CONSORT, TRIPOD+AI…).
skills.auditFooter: The approach is cited in the literature on self-improving AI as the response to a known failure: self-critique inherits the blind spots that produce confident fabrication.
